notes.VFM_05_Launch: The selected Bubble Blaster carries the launch velocity in the hand. Compare the existing Launch Arc with a projectile catapult and a human catapult. The enlarged fountain runs ballistic trajectories and pauses its own clock near the apex; the museum continues running.
notes.VFM_03_Motion: The mower applies the earlier projection to work: integrate the nominal drawn force along the actual displacement. Its force is a declared model value, not a measurement of pressure from the hand.
notes.Vectors_Act3_FieldsAndMotion: The upgraded Wind Room drives rigid cubes and familiar points with relative-velocity drag. Aim a held rose point to steer the air, or use the controls at the entry. Walk through the same field. Compare the older Force Vortex, which prescribes a spiral velocity and ejects the visitor, with the primary vortex that integrates acceleration.
notes.Vectors_Act4a_KineticForces: Viscosity Layers returns the drag comparison at bench scale. The centrifuge adds a circular hand ride: hold the rose handle, travel around the ring, release into the tangent. It prescribes the circular motion; it does not simulate a physical hinge or rotate the tracked head.
notes.Vectors_Act4b_Oscillation: Compare the physical 6DOF SpringSuspension joint, now pulled with a rose hand grip, with Spring Tower, whose cosine animation illustrates a period. The existing coupled PointBody springs remain the tutorial object.
notes.VFM_07_Gravity: Orbit Walk is a prescribed two-body barycentre diagram. It is a controlled comparison beside the primary mutually attracting points, whose trajectories are integrated.
notes.VFM_08_Arena: Compare two presentations: Momentum Cradle shows ideal input/output poses; Newton's Cradle integrates pendulum angles with an idealized equal-mass collision exchange. Neither is the Jolt collision solver used by bowling.
